text: Testing is a crucial part of building good software, and it usually happens at different levels. First, developers write unit tests to check individual functions or components in isolation. Then, integration tests verify that these different parts work together correctly as a whole system. A popular approach is test-driven development, where you write a failing test first, then write just enough code to make it pass, and finally refactor. While this takes more time at the start, it builds strong confidence. Knowing that automated tests cover your code means you can make changes and add new features without constantly worrying about breaking something that already worked.
